system.summary: Numerical syllable-and-word code (the = 1385), about 1,600 numbers; 1-100 mostly whole words; values climb alphabetically only in short runs, then break; superscript o = plural, a mark under a group modifies it.
system.sibling_key: Armstrong's THE=972 code (targets/armstrong/), which Madison's editors said JQA used; tested and ruled out. Pinkney's London code named in Smith's 1809 instructions (Ford 3:327-28) not tested.
system.notes: distinct_symbols = numbers in code_table.tsv (22 Sept 2026: 391 H, 241 C, 311 M, 19 I), built by consolidate.py from pairs_jqa.txt, clerk_*.tsv (interlinear decodes on frames 0048, 0182, 0183, 0184, 0185, 0189, 0190, 0194, 0198, 0206), ford_pairs*.tsv (39 coded 1811 blocks aligned with Ford vol. 4) and slot_inferences.tsv. Homophones: several words have two groups (those 551/651, English 1291/1292, with 1190/1192-era variants, few 329/350). separation is as transcribed; the manuscript uses dots and spaces.

prior_solution.where: Ford printed both No. 88 passages as not decyphered; the clerk's decode on frame 0206 covers only the rest of the despatch. No other reading found. Ford vol. 4 prints the Department's decipherments of OTHER 1811 despatches in the same code; those were used as known plaintext to rebuild the code (22 Sept 2026), not as a reading of No. 88.

conditions.human_role: Project-level: set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5 and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.
tools: align.py (DP alignment of code groups with Ford's printed plaintext)

solution.what: Checked the Madison editors' claim that JQA used Armstrong's THE=972 code against Ford 3:327-28 and 3:370.
Fetched NARA M35 reels 2 and 3 frames and scored them for code texture (codescore.py).
Applied the 592-entry Armstrong THE=972 table to JQA's 1812 despatches: noise; his code has the = 1385, of = 1576.
Read the clerk's interlinear decodes on frames 0206 and 0189 into pairs_jqa.txt (262 clerk-attested pairs).
Worked out the code's structure: alphabetical blocks of about 50 numbers, shuffled, whole words in 1-100.
Filled groups by slot inference inside the blocks and context (48 I and 93 M pairs).
Ford's nine undecyphered lines (gap88.txt) read 124 of 134 groups: Rumyantsev's strokes at Wilna and the false report of his death.
The remainder on frame 0207 (rem88.txt) renders 212 of 250 complete groups, in threads only.

Located the images of NARA M35 reel 3 in the main checkout (img03, downloaded 18 Sept) and surveyed the contact sheets: interlinear clerk decodes on frames 0048, 0182-0185, 0190, 0194, 0198, 0211 and later; 'decyphered' sheets for 1811 despatches (0011, 0037, 0064, 0067, 0072, 0082, 0092, ...).

Read the clerk's interlinear decodes on frames 0182 (No. 80, 29 Feb 1812) and 0048 (top) by hand, and on 0183R, 0184, 0185, 0190, 0194R, 0198R with two transcription agents: ~2,000 pairs (1,296 H, 869 M) in clerk_*.tsv.

Transcribed 39 coded blocks of 1811 despatches (frames 0005-0132) and aligned them with the plaintext Ford printed from the Department's decipherments (Writings vol. 4) using align.py, checked by eye: 589 C and 270 M pairs in ford_pairs*.tsv.
Merged all sources into one table (consolidate.py, overrides.tsv for 40 disputed numbers): 962 numbers, 391 H, 241 C, 311 M, 19 I. The alphabetical order holds only in short runs.
Re-read the No. 88 groups from zoomed crops of frames 0206 and 0207: three digits corrected (168, 1426, 302) and a catchword (1102) removed; 1081 in the remainder line 5 is blurred.

Alphabetical-slot bracketing of the groups still unread (slots.py): nine grade-I values (168 ey, 1434 journ, 83 opposition, 143 mod, 815 def, 239 sive, 108 comply, 432 net, 726 rate); 1575 and 1540, first slot-inferred as off and along, were then attested by Ford as adv and ambass.

No. 88 re-measured with measure.py and a sense-flag file (sense88.tsv): 379 of 390 groups valued, 355 read as sense (0.910); Ford's nine lines 127/133 (0.955), the remainder 228/257 (0.887). Before this session: 336 of 391 valued (0.859), sense not measured.

Clerk interlinear decodes read on frames 0047, 0048 (rest), 0210-0211, 0247 (560 pairs; clerk_0047.tsv etc.); 0056-57 found to be a clear decyphered copy of No. 46; 220 = probab (three clerk readings) replaces proper.

Coded blocks of eight despatches Oct 1811-Sept 1812 transcribed and aligned with Ford vol. 4; No. 95 aligned against the Department's clear copy on 0230-0232 (1,926 pairs; ford1812_pairs*.tsv): 996 = fri (friendship), 1457+ = ll (Chancellor), 83 = opposition, 1061 = cu, 588 = tled.

No. 88 re-read on zoomed crops of 0206R and 0207: 792 not 492 (by), 1061 not 1081 (e-va-cu-ation), 588 not 888 (bat-tle), 1384 not 1385 (that); 570 and 1099 confirmed; the 7 line-end groups are cut by the binding gutter.

Alphabetical-slot inferences (grade I) for the remaining groups: 1403 ib and 350 fl (in-fl-ex-ib-ly, inflexibly), 1309 bat (battle of Friedland), 426 negotiate, 1540 along; 927 pire from context only.
measure.py: 375 of 390 groups read as sense (0.962), gap88 0.970, rem88 0.957; open: 7 gutter-cut groups, im-pas-sion-ed (JQA slip for impaired), 1508, 1185, 570, 748.
rem88 l.19 re-read: 1097 sho (last digit overwritten 9->7) and 1383 than (5/3 overwritten), both M: "than along the sho-res of the Baltic"; 748 res now reads. 376/390 = 0.964.

Five more 1811-1812 despatches aligned with Ford (Nos. 71, 72, 74, 75, 81; ford1812_pairs_b.tsv): JQA's own 'un-im-pa-ir-ed' in No. 83 (1477 1424 1102 1435 520) and his catchword 1102 show that No. 88's 1112 1433 are copying slips; the phrase reads 'had not been impaired'. 1185, 1508 not found; 570 = tol(d) confirmed four more times.
measure.py: 380 of 390 groups read as sense (0.974): gap88 133/133, rem88 247/257; open: 7 gutter-cut groups (needs the original), 1508, 1185, 570.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 380 tokens, 207 types, en-modern order 4: reading -1.962 per letter; random keys -2.897 (z 9.0); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -1.989 (mean -2.005, z 3.5); annealer on the real text -2.002. Verdict: pass.

Profile content unchanged.

Integration check of PR #596: we028_measure.py re-run (1,742 pairs, 0.932, shuffled maximum 0.044; with exact matches only 1,528 of 1,742 = 0.877; 423 distinct codes); an own decoder from the sheet CSV gives every sheet value of we028_no88.tsv (390 rows: 369 sure, 15 probable, 3 restored, 3 unresolved); frame 0207 fetched from the National Archives Catalog and lines 8-12 and 14-17 of the remainder compared (about 95 groups agree with rem88.txt apart from the two corrections, 262 and 649, which are right on the image). Image check of the seven groups one digit away from the sheet value the sense wants (proposed by Brice Dudout, PR #596). Frames 0206 and 0207 fetched again from the National Archives Catalog (NAID 188725601) and each group enlarged. 1864: the image reads 1864 (closed 8; wanted 1364 tain). 669: reads 669 (wanted 569 to). 588: 5, a one-loop digit that is 6 or 8, 8 (wanted 568 tle). 508: reads 508 (wanted 518 ect). 818: first digit with a closed lower loop, 8 likelier than a blotted 5 (wanted 518 ect). 1575: reads 1575 (wanted 1515 adv). 1585: third digit overwritten, not told (wanted 1535 al), and the word lacks ex. No misreading of ours among them; the slips are the writer's. New: the left leaf of 0206 runs into the gutter, and the stroke of a further group follows 908 (Chancellor's ... and advice); counted as one lost word. rem88.txt (262, 649), pairs_jqa.txt, overrides.tsv and code_table.tsv (252 str, 549 min, 927 pire, thither withdrawn) brought into line with the sheet.

One-digit rule applied (owner's decision of 14 Nov 2026, README Conventions: surviving period key, one digit changed, inside a word whose other groups are read from the key). Key: the M97 roll 13 sheet. Read under the rule: certainly (1864), battle (588/568), directly (508), expectation (818), advice (1575). Not covered: to (669, a whole word), Alexander (1585, digit not legible and the word incomplete). Recount in words: remainder 164 of 177 = 0.927 (was 0.910), nine lines 97 of 100 = 0.970 (was 95 of 99 = 0.960). The remainder stays under 95%, held back by six words on gutter-cut groups: class read in part kept.

Decrypt audit of the two No. 88 texts: code_table.tsv re-applied to gap88.txt and rem88.txt and compared with the readings in texts/ (33 of 261 compared words depart), then by hand with the sheet values of we028_no88.tsv. Found: the readings follow the code sheet since 14 Nov 2026 while the profile named only the rebuilt table (428 neither, 143 moderate, 632 media, 1157 possib, 948 Russia ...); clear words inside the code lines are counted by the script as supplied; spellings are modernised; the transcriptions do not carry the plural and doubling marks that NOTES documents (1457 ll, 908 's, 1535 all); eight words stand in the readings without a bracket where the groups as transcribed give something else and no file says why (a second "it", events, all, affairs, disclosed, system, proposition for, making to), and "impaired" for im-pas-ion-ed is documented but not bracketed. key_we028_no88.tsv added (209 groups, sheet values copied from we028_no88.tsv, checked against the sheet transcription in morris1813) and listed in outcome.key_file. With the sheet key 29 of 260 words depart; the script's own figure stays 33 of 261 because it prefers the table. The film was not looked at.

Marking round of the decrypt audit: ten places bracketed in the two No. 88 readings without changing a letter (nine lines: impa[ir]ed, [it], al[l], event[s], affair[s]; remainder: disclose[d], sy[st]em, proposi[tion], mak[ing], [to]), and a sentence added to each file's head comment. Hole rate (v2_score.py): nine lines 0.039 to 0.088, remainder 0.079 to 0.107. The word counts and read shares were not redone; whether any of the ten is a mark on the film was not checked.

Leads 992 and 991 (Andrew Beling, with AI agents). Frames 0168, 0170-0171, 0196, 0197 of NARA M35 reel 3 fetched from the National Archives Catalog; every code group of No. 85 (0196 left, 0197 left) and No. 74 (0168, both leaves) and the clerk's decyphered sheet of No. 74 transcribed twice by agents blind to each other, to any table and to this folder: 796 tokens, the same number at 717, doubted by neither at 600.

No. 85: 0.929 and 0.911 (largest control 0.062); No. 74: 0.935 and 0.932 (largest control 0.131). Passed, one run.

Frame 0196 lines 11-16: 51 of 55 words, a second reading of the lines first read on 22 Sept 2026 (five numbers stand on the film with sheet values that give no sense: 1236, 209, 49, 1501, 820). No. 74: the three groups the clerk marked 'Error in Cypher' (387 1431 1101) are sue, into, P on the sheet: is-sue into P-russia; no number needs changing.

A third agent read frame 0197 and the first eight groups of frame 0168 from its own enlargements before opening the sheet or the transcriptions: its blind reading agreed at every group of 0197 except the last of the two lines (first 528, on a second look 548), leaving 116x, 891/841 and the gutter group open as the transcribers did; the same reading of both runs (it proposed ex-plain-ed, 1138, where ex-pound-ed, 1160, had been proposed; both are recorded, the word is a hole), and 'P-russia' on 0168. It read 887 where the clerk's sheet has 387, so 'issue' rests on the clerk's figures. Ten numbers of the test detail checked against frame 0196: nine as the file says, one clerk's word misplaced by a transcriber.

Ford 4:270, 338-339 prints the gaps; Internet Archive full-text search on three phrases of the clear text beside them returns only copies of Ford's volume; Founders Online has no result for 'neutrality of Sweden' or 'suffered to remain open'. JQA's letterbook copy (Adams Papers reel 136, MHS) not seen.

Recount of the three No. 85 readings under README Conventions (16 Nov 2026: a word with a supplied or emended letter is a hole): intention[s], expectation[s], objection[s] (s supplied from the plural mark) and los[s] (the sheet gives lose) are now holes. Held-out test of code_table.tsv on Adams's despatches of 1810 (Andrew Beling, with AI agents; beling1810/). Plan and pass mark hashed before the run (agreement >= 0.80 and >= best of 100 shuffled tables + 0.30). 22 coded passages of Nos. 21, 23, 24, 25, 27 and 28 (NARA M35 reel 2, 3,083 groups, our first transcriptions) aligned with align.py, unchanged, against their independent plaintexts (Ford 3:469; the period decipherments on frames 156-159, 169-172, 178-179, 184). Blind second transcriptions by helper agents agree with the first at 0.716 (No. 24) and 0.751 (No. 29); No. 24 rescored post hoc on its second transcription: 0.814. No. 29 has no witness and is not scored. The table is not changed.

The table is not changed.
